name: html-elements

description.en: 55 everyday elements of HTML, the markup language of the web: the front says in plain words what an element is for, in English and Swedish, and the back gives its tag, such as <a> or <main>. Covers the document and its metadata, sections, text, lists, images and media, tables and forms; obsolete elements are left out. Based on the WHATWG HTML Living Standard (CC BY 4.0), with every card checked against MDN Web Docs and Wikidata.
description.sv: 55 vanliga element i HTML, webbens märkspråk: på framsidan står med vanliga ord vad ett element används till, på engelska och svenska, och på baksidan dess tagg, till exempel <a> eller <main>. Täcker dokumentet och dess metadata, avsnitt, text, listor, bilder och media, tabeller och formulär; föråldrade element är utelämnade. Bygger på WHATWG:s HTML Living Standard (CC BY 4.0), och varje kort är kontrollerat mot MDN Web Docs och Wikidata.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

The standard. 18 pages of the multipage edition of the WHATWG HTML Living Standard (the front page, the indices, the chapters that define the chosen elements and the chapter on obsolete features) were downloaded on 2026-10-04 (fetch_whatwg.sh; the front page says 'Living Standard — Last Updated 4 October 2026'), with the Acknowledgements page (licence notice), the rendering chapter (default CSS) and the link types chapter. The index of elements (indices.html#elements-3, 111 rows: h1–h6 share one row, and MathML math, SVG svg and autonomous custom elements are also listed) was extracted with elements_index.py. Obsolete and non-conforming elements are not in that index; they are listed in the chapter 'Obsolete features' (obsolete.html, section 16.2 'Non-conforming features'), which was converted to text and read to confirm that none of the chosen elements is listed there; its advice 'acronym: Use abbr instead' is the source of the abbr note.

Selection. From the index 55 elements were chosen that a web author meets every day, in seven groups: the document and its metadata (html, head, title, link, meta, style, body, script), sections (main, header, footer, nav, article, section, aside, h1), grouping content (p, hr, pre, blockquote, ol, ul, li, figure, figcaption, div), text (a, em, strong, q, abbr, code, sub, sup, mark, time, br, span), embedded content (img, iframe, video, audio, canvas), tables (table, tr, td, th) and forms and interactive elements (form, input, button, label, select, textarea, details, dialog). Each candidate had to be describable in plain words so that only one element of the standard answers the description; elements that failed that test, or that only make sense next to another, were left out (see Selection).

Definitions. For each element its section in the standard (the id the-<element>-element) was read and the defining sentence extracted with spec_represents.py; where the section does not open with '<element> represents' (link, style, script, the headings, sub/sup, video, canvas) the defining sentence was found with grep_rest.sh. Facts used on the fronts or in the notes beyond the definition (for example that div is 'an element of last resort', that the header may hold a search form or logos, that a document has at most one main without the hidden attribute, the examples given for sub and sup, the default rendering of em, strong, pre, ol, ul, hr and q) were looked up with grep_claims.sh, grep_notes.sh, grep_more.sh and in the rendering chapter converted to text (to_text.py). Every card's first evidence entry quotes the sentences used inside quotation marks; where it adds a rule from the rendering chapter, an example, a content model or the index's one-line description, that part is labelled with where it comes from and quoted separately (see Quality control, round 3).

Fronts. Each front says what the element is for in plain words, written in plain words from the standard's definition; several keep the standard's own key words (for example 'stress emphasis', 'strong importance, seriousness or urgency', 'a data cell in a table', 'thematic break', 'disclosure widget'), which is why the deck is CC BY 4.0 (see Licensing). Where an element alone would be a hard guess, the front adds an example taken from the standard (a blog or forum post for article, a scene change for hr, x₁₀ and E = mc² for sub and sup, a postal address for br). The back is the start tag in angle brackets, with no attributes, tagged as text in no language (zxx).

Ambiguity checks. Every front was compared with the index's descriptions of all the other elements, chosen or not, to make sure it fits exactly one. Close pairs were separated on purpose: head (metadata) versus header (introductory content) and body (all contents) versus main (the main content); section versus div versus article; blockquote (a block) versus q (in the running text); em versus strong versus mark; div versus span; td versus th; label (caption of a form control) versus the omitted legend (caption of a fieldset); button (labelled by its content) versus input buttons (labelled by their value attribute); img versus picture, which the index describes with the same word 'Image' (picture is a container that offers sources to an img, so 'An image' is img, and the note says so); ul versus menu (a toolbar of commands, named in the note); iframe versus object (the index calls iframe a 'Child navigable' and object an 'Image, child navigable, or plugin'; the front says 'frame', and the note gives the name 'inline frame'). Only h1 of the six heading elements is in the deck, because fronts for h2–h6 would differ only by a level number.

Cross-check against MDN (verification). For every element the source of its MDN Web Docs page (mdn/content on GitHub, files/en-us/web/html/reference/elements/<element>/index.md) was downloaded (fetch_mdn.sh) and its first paragraph and status flags printed (mdn_summary.py). Every card's MDN summary agreed with the standard's definition and the front, and no page carries a deprecated or non-standard flag. The second evidence entry of each card quotes MDN's first sentence. No wording or selection was taken from MDN: fronts that came close to MDN's wording in the first draft (title, textarea, span) were reworded from the standard instead (see Quality control).

Cross-check against Wikidata. A SPARQL query (q1.rq) found the Wikidata item of every element of the deck as an instance of a subclass of 'HTML element' (Q179551); wd_items.py then read each item's short name (P1813) and 'described at URL' (P973). Every one of the 55 items has P1813 equal to the tag name and a P973 link to the very section of the standard used for the card, so each card has two Wikidata checks that the builder runs against live Wikidata: P1813 = the tag and P973 = the section's URL. Two items (meta, dialog) carry a second, unrelated P973 URL besides the standard's; the checks test only the standard's URL.

Swedish. The Swedish fronts and notes are translations of the English fronts and notes. Swedish terms that carry the meaning were checked against Swedish dictionaries and Wikidata: in Svensk ordbok or SAOL via the svenska.se search API (svenska.py): hyperlänk, stycke, rubrik, sidfot, radbrytning, förkortning, akronym, dialogruta, rullgardinsmeny, upphöjd, formulär, bildtext, maskinläsbar, fristående, betoning, sökträff, scenbyte, tabell, webbsida, programkod; and as Swedish labels or aliases of Wikidata items (wd_search.py), each then made a label check on its card: hyperlänk (Q102014), stycke (Q194431), rubrik (Q3529597), sidfot (Q526434), förkortning (Q102786), akronym (Q101244), dialogruta and dialogfönster (Q86915), rullgardinsmeny (Q783066), metadata (Q180160), teckenkodning (Q184759), citat (Q206287), tabell (Q496946), webbsida (Q36774), programkod (Q128751), knapp (Q1335171) and Kryssruta (Q23544, written kryssruta in running text). Words not found in either dictionary and not in Wikidata (stilmall, sidospalt, bitmapp, löptext) were avoided; the remaining compounds (rotelement, datacell, rubrikcell, formulärfält, formulärkontroll, navigeringslänkar, videospelare, ljudström, rityta, spelgrafik, textfält) are ordinary Swedish compounds of dictionary words. The other words looked up gave these results: skript (SO: 'instruktioner eller kommandon till datorprogram'; used on canvas), etikett (SO: 'lapp (som sätts fast på vara) som anger en varas namn, innehåll m.m.'; used on label and button in the transferred sense of the text that names a form control), bokmärke (SO entry; used on title in the sense of a saved link), navigering (SAOL entry; used in navigeringslänkar on nav), nedsänkt (no entry of its own: SAOL returns the verb nedsänka, whose past participle it is; kept on sub as the counterpart of upphöjd), initialord (SO and SAOL entries; not used), modal and flik (entries, but in senses unrelated to user interfaces; not used). Element and attribute names (title, base, link, style, script, type, value, <summary>) stay in their English form because they are typed literally.

Everything was written into this dossier with gen.py from the card data, built with the builder (scripts/authored_decks.py build html-elements, which ran all Wikidata checks against live Wikidata) and validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts html-elements). The fixes from the independent review rounds 1–3 were applied directly to this dossier with fix_qc1.py (recorded under queries) and the deck was built and validated again.
selection: 55 elements of the HTML Living Standard (WHATWG), last updated 4 October 2026: , , , <link>, <meta>, <style>, <body>, <script>, <main>, <header>, <footer>, <nav>, <article>, <section>, <aside>, <h1>, <p>, <hr>, <pre>, <blockquote>, <ol>, <ul>, <li>, <figure>, <figcaption>, <div>, <a>, <em>, <strong>, <q>, <abbr>, <code>, <sub>, <sup>, <mark>, <time>, <br>, <span>, <img>, <iframe>, <video>, <audio>, <canvas>, <table>, <tr>, <td>, <th>, <form>, <input>, <button>, <label>, <select>, <textarea>, <details>, <dialog>. Included: elements from the standard's index of elements that web authors use every day and that can be described in plain words so that exactly one element fits. Left out: everything obsolete or non-conforming (the standard lists those, such as applet, acronym, center, font, marquee, big, frame, strike and tt, only in section 16.2 of its chapter 'Obsolete features', not in the index); h2–h6, whose fronts would differ from h1 only by a number; elements whose purpose cannot be told apart from a chosen element without technical detail, or that only make sense as the child of another element: b, i, u, s, small, cite, dfn, var, samp, kbd, data, bdi, bdo, wbr, ins, del, ruby, rt, rp (text-level elements whose distinctions are subtle), tbody, thead, tfoot, col, colgroup, caption (table parts), optgroup, option, datalist, selectedcontent, legend, fieldset, output, progress, meter (further form parts), source, track, picture, map, area, embed, object (further embedded content), summary, menu, search, hgroup, address, dl, dt, dd, base, noscript, template and slot; and the foreign elements MathML math and SVG svg and autonomous custom elements. Several omitted elements (<menu>, <picture>, <summary>) are named in back notes where they help to tell a pair apart, as are elements of other cards (<a>, <link>, <input type="submit">). The selection is this deck's own, not copied from a list.

# Download the WHATWG HTML Living Standard multipage chapters used for the deck.

done

queries.purpose: Print the standard's index of elements (element | description) and its 'Last Updated' date; run as uv run --with beautifulsoup4 --with html5lib python3 <scratch>/elements_index.py > <scratch>/elements_index.txt (111 rows)
queries.query:
"""Print the WHATWG 'List of elements' table (indices.html#elements-3): element | description,
and the licence and date lines of the spec's front page.
Run: uv run --with beautifulsoup4 --with html5lib python3 <scratch>/elements_index.py"""
import pathlib, re
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
D = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "whatwg"
soup = BeautifulSoup((D / "indices.html").read_text(), "html5lib")
h = soup.find(id="elements-3")
table = h.find_next("table")
for tr in table.find("tbody").find_all("tr"):
    th = tr.find("th"); tds = tr.find_all("td")
    print(" ".join(th.get_text(" ").split()), "|", " ".join(tds[0].get_text(" ").split()))
idx = BeautifulSoup((D / "index.html").read_text(), "html5lib")
txt = " ".join(idx.get_text(" ").split())
for pat in [r"Living Standard — Last Updated [^—]{0,40}", r"Copyright © [^.]*\.[^.]*\.[^.]*\.[^.]*\."]:
    for m in re.finditer(pat, txt):
        print("INDEX:", m.group(0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Download the MDN Web Docs source (mdn/content on GitHub) of each element page, and MDN's licence page.
set -u
D="$(dirname "$0")/mdn"
mkdir -p "$D"
UA="solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
for e in html head title link meta style body script main header footer nav article section aside heading_elements p hr pre blockquote ol ul li figure figcaption div a em strong q abbr code sub sup mark time br span img iframe video audio canvas table tr td th form input button label select textarea details dialog b i menu search picture object embed caption fieldset legend; do
  code=$(curl -sS -A "$UA" -o "$D/$e.md" -w '%{http_code}' "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/content/main/files/en-us/web/html/reference/elements/$e/index.md")
  echo "$e $code"
done
curl -sS -A "$UA" -o "$D/licence.html" "https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/MDN/Writing_guidelines/Attrib_copyright_license"

queries.purpose: Print each MDN page's status flags and first paragraph; run as python3 <scratch>/mdn_summary.py
queries.query:
"""For each downloaded MDN element page print the front-matter status flags and the first paragraph
(the summary) after the front matter. Run: python3 <scratch>/mdn_summary.py"""
import pathlib, re, sys
D = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "mdn"
for f in sorted(D.glob("*.md")):
    s = f.read_text()
    fm, body = s.split("---", 2)[1], s.split("---", 2)[2]
    status = re.findall(r"^\s+- (deprecated|experimental|non-standard)", fm, re.M)
    paras = [p.strip() for p in body.split("\n\n") if p.strip() and not p.strip().startswith("{{")]
    print(f"{f.stem} status={status or 'none'}\n  {' '.join(paras[0].split())}\n")

"""Look up Swedish words in Svensk ordbok (SO) and SAOL via the svenska.se search API and print
whether each word has an entry and the entry's first definition(s). Raw responses saved under svenska/.
Run: python3 <scratch>/svenska.py <word>...
URL: https://svenska.se/api/search/{so|saol}?q=<word>&exactMatch=true"""

UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"

        url = f"https://svenska.se/api/search/{dic}?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": w, "exactMatch": "true"})

        for h in hits:
            for hb in h["_source"].get("huvudbetydelser", []) or []:
